record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; result files are listed but their contents were not provided.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a residual-stream activation patch and refusal outcomes. This is a different intervention from the difference-in-means direction and ablation described in V1, but tests whether an activation intervention changes refusal behavior.
record.gate_note: The README reports results for the cross-model, same-prompt patch. The listed summary and detailed-results files are not available to inspect; no results from them are inferred.
record.test_reason: The repo patches a per-prompt, same-prompt delta (h_base − α·h_chat) into one layer of Llama-2-7B-Chat. It never computes, ablates or adds a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. The intervention is a prompt-specific, full-activation shift toward the base model, not a single direction. So its refusal drop says nothing about whether one direction mediates refusal (V1), and nothing about direction transfer from base to chat (V6). The original paper is not cited. The result is a related steering finding, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The README says the layer-11, α=0.7 patch substantially reduces refusal on the selected toxic prompts while benign refusal stays unchanged, with moderate KL drift. The authors also say larger α raises acceptance and drift, and that the patch is prompt-conditioned and layer-local. They frame it as a steering study, not a safety system.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a per-prompt, same-prompt cross-model activation delta at one layer, rather than a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction projected out across layers and positions. The repo presents a steering demonstration, not a reproduction of the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: The README gives results at layer 11 and α=0.7 and says larger α increases acceptance but also drift; it calls α∈[0.3, 0.7] a reasonable range. No separate numerical sweep results are stated in the provided text.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama-2-7B-Chat, patching layer 11 with h_base − 0.7·h_chat for the same prompt cuts refusal from 0.99 to 0.09. The 100 OR-Bench prompts were selected so that chat refuses and base answers. Benign refusal stays at 0.01, with mean benign KL of 3.96.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Chat-model refusal can be largely removed by steering one mid layer's activations toward the base model's activations on the same prompt.

record.problems: Only README results are available here; the listed result files were not provided. No uncertainty estimates or controls are stated. Benign refusal and KL do not establish that general capabilities are largely intact.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows extracted: the README points to detailed_results.json and other result files, but their contents are unavailable in the provided text.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is extracted, ablated or added. There is no capability benchmark.
No jailbreak analysis and no adversarial training.
No comparison of one direction with several directions or an affine account.
Harmfulness judgment is not measured separately from refusal.
Base activations are used per prompt, but no direction is extracted, so transfer of a direction is not tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README is available; the summary and detailed result files were not provided. There is no uncertainty, no control direction and no sweep numbers. The reader's T2/tests classification is rejected because the intervention is not the claimed direction.

versions.untested_parts: The repo does not find or ablate a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, test all layers and positions, or add the direction to induce refusals. The reported benign refusal rate is not a general-capability evaluation.
No weight edit or abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of one direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
The patch uses a base-model activation on the same prompt, but does not test whether the claimed difference-in-means direction transfers across models, languages, or training stages.
No refusal-training method or stage is compared.
